script.description: Normalize dot_number into the canonical unpadded string carriers uses, so auth-history-enrichment-policy can join. FMCSA zero-pads dot_number to eight characters in auth_history.csv ('00023680') and does not pad it in carriers.csv ('23680'). An enrich index coerces every field to keyword regardless of the source mapping and reindexes _source verbatim, so the rendered string is what the join compares -- and '00023680' never matches '23680'. This join previously worked only by accident: the loader inferred the column as int64 and discarded the padding before Elasticsearch saw it, so both sides happened to agree. Reading CSVs faithfully as strings removed that accident and took carriers' auth_history enrichment from 546,042 documents to zero, which is how this processor came to exist. Assigns a String rather than a Long because the string is the actual join key: emitting a Long left this side putting a JSON integer into its enrich index while out-of-service-orders put an untouched CSV string into its own, two shapes that agree digit for digit only as long as nothing perturbs either. Mirrors every other dot_number pipeline; strips at the decimal point too, since a NaN elsewhere in a column still widens it to float64. A value that will not parse is left untouched and unjoinable rather than failing the document -- see tests/test_dot_number_join_contract.py.
script.source: if (ctx.dot_number == null) { return; } String raw = String.valueOf(ctx.dot_number); int dot = raw.indexOf('.'); if (dot >= 0) { raw = raw.substring(0, dot); } if (raw.isEmpty()) { return; } ctx.dot_number = String.valueOf(Long.parseLong(raw));
